messages:
alicia: Ran a full nsys + perfetto sweep on the FP8/int8 mixed workload this morning. nsys timeline shows repeated CPU-side dequant task bursts right before GPU kernel launches — looks like a "bridge" path that moves tensors through host memory. attaching trace: https://perfetto.link/abc123 :eyes:

alicia: excerpt from timeline: 
[GPU] kernel: attn_fwd_int8    start=12.8ms  duration=0.42ms
[CPU] host: dequant_cpu_stage    start=12.9ms  duration=9.8ms  (memcpy H2D queued)
[GPU] kernel: attn_fwd_fp8    start=22.8ms  duration=0.58ms
queueing stalls ~= 9.8ms per request, correlates with throughput drop

sanjay: wow that's huge. can you paste the nsys command you used? want to repro locally.

alicia: sure — command: 
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --output=fp8_kv_sweep.nsys ./run_e2e.sh --batch 8 --pbatch 16
nsys export -t sqlite fp8_kv_sweep.nsys
perfetto --attach perfetto_trace.pb // uploaded link above
```

kevin: first-pass hypothesis: kernel selection is falling back to an unfused dequant + cudaMemcpy path when sequence-length distribution triggers a fallback quantized kernel. that fallback is CPU-side in our current kernel table for some model shapes.

kevin: also saw related KV-cache churn in the same window — batching mixes long-prefix and short-prefix requests which causes frequent KV evictions, forcing re-materialization and dequant for many requests.

emily: re: KV thrash — flamechart shows repeated small allocations at the tail of the KV ring buffer, eviction count spikes when seq_len variance > ~40. grouping by seq_len bin dramatically reduces evictions in a small test.

alicia: i repro'd that locally by replaying a mix: 20% seq=2048, 80% seq=256. when we shuffle batches random, eviction rate x3. if we bucket by seq len, eviction drops ~70% and the CPU dequant bursts disappear in nsys.

kevin: good. short-term mitigation: change batching heuristic to prefer homogeneous seq_len within a scheduling window, and add a KV TTL so recently-used KV stays pinned for N batches. mid-term: remove host-side dequant path by registering fused gpu-only kernels for those shapes.

perf-bot: regression alert: perf/throughput decreased 11% on CI for commit c3f4b2d (model-onnx-mapping change). linked nsys artifact: s3://redwood-perf/fp8/c3f4b2d.nsys

sanjay: could the ONNX mapping change have altered op fusion decisions and forced fallback to CPU dequant? looks plausible.

kevin: yes, mapping changed op ordering for attn QKV split, which prevented our cuda-fused dequant path from matching. that explains the regression signal.

emily: actionable checklist: 
1) revert the ONNX mapping change on a canary branch and re-run the CI nsys -> compare. (owner: sanjay)
2) add seq_len binning to batching policy (owner: alicia)
3) implement a soft-KV-TTL to reduce eviction thrash (owner: kevin)
4) add unit test covering fused-dequant kernel pattern matching in the kernel registry (owner: emily)

alicia: i can pick up seq_len binning today. starting with a cheap heuristic: sort queued requests by seq_len per 50ms window. should be low-risk.

kevin: for fused kernel matching i have a small patch that relaxes op-order strictness, will open PR and include a microbench. expect 10-20% latency win for the affected shapes once applied.

alicia: thanks — i'll run a new nsys after your PR lands. leaving trace links and raw sqlite in the thread for anyone wanting to dig: s3://redwood-traces/1792345600/

sanjay: fyi i'll also run a perfetto capture with CPU stacks to see if memcpy originates from our runtime or from libtorch/ONNX glue.

kevin: one more note: dequant memcpy shows up as pageable H2D in the driver timeline. if confirmed, we should force pinned allocations for dequant temp buffers to avoid extra copy. small change but high impact.

alicia: agreed. pinned allocations + seq_len binning should be our v1 mitigations. will report back with updated nsys within 24h. :thumbsup:
